title: Brookfield Private Wealth — Retail RIA Aggregator & Delegated Advisor Scoping
initialRequestBrief: Brookfield signed a statement of work for its private wealth feeder fund: about 2,500 high-net-worth investors onboarded through wealth advisors at independent RIA firms, with go-live on 23 February 2026 ahead of the fund's first monthly close on 1 March. Sales scoped six weeks using the institutional onboarding template. Brookfield's home-office team will coordinate the advisors, and account types include individual, joint, IRA and revocable trust accounts.
summary: Sales scoping used the institutional template and underestimated delivery by four weeks, because wealth advisors needed 1-to-many delegated preparation across 40+ HNW accounts each, bulk intake and per-account-type signing. A phased delivery saved the first close, and the team produced a private wealth scoping rubric with an effort multiplier and a delegated advisor access matrix.
howItWent: The SOW quoted six weeks on the institutional template, which assumes one investor, one signer and one form. Discovery a week later showed about 60 advisors at 9 RIA firms with a median of 42 accounts each, expecting to prepare subscriptions in bulk and send them for client signature, which the investor-owned collaboration model could not do. Rather than slip the first close, Sales agreed a change order: phase 1 (advisor delegation and single-account preparation) on 23 February and phase 2 (bulk intake and IRA custodian routing) on 23 March. Phase 1 surfaced one access bug: an advisor who changed firms still saw his former firm's clients because his rep-code link was not end-dated. Delivery finished four weeks after the original date, and Brookfield's March close went through with 1,140 advisor-prepared subscriptions.
resolutionSteps: Build the Private Wealth / RIA Pre-Sales Scoping Rubric & Effort Multiplier: ask who prepares subscriptions, how many advisors and accounts per advisor, which account types and whether bulk intake is needed, before quoting.

Standardize the Delegated Financial Advisor Role-Based Access Matrix: advisor scope from the active rep code, assistants without attestation rights, home-office oversight without edit rights, and no advisor signing for clients.
Re-evaluate advisor access nightly and on every transfer event so an advisor who changes firms loses the previous firm's clients immediately.
When the first close is fixed, phase delivery: delegation and single-account preparation first, then bulk intake and custodian routing.

pitfalls.warning: The institutional scoping template asks how many investors there are, never who fills in the forms. Delegated advisor preparation changes the access model and the estimate.
pitfalls.author: ryan.miller

pitfalls.warning: Advisor access tied to a rep code must be end-dated on transfer; otherwise an advisor who changes firms keeps seeing the old firm's clients.
pitfalls.author: sarah.tran

pitfalls.warning: Never let an advisor sign on a client's behalf; route powers of attorney to GP review as an exception.
pitfalls.author: sarah.tran

pitfalls.warning: IRA subscriptions need the custodian's acceptance after the investor signs; leaving custodial routing to the end of the project blocks those accounts at close.
pitfalls.author: chloe.nguyen

artifacts.description: Pre-sales scoping rubric for private wealth and RIA deals: discovery questions, effort multiplier on the institutional baseline, access-model defaults, phasing pattern and the Brookfield worked example.
Role-based access matrix for delegated wealth advisors: home office, advisor, assistant, investor, IRA custodian, GP investor relations and transferred advisor, across 14 permissions.
